name: Pane
title: Ninebrains vs Pane
description: Ninebrains vs Pane (RunPane by Dcouple): two open-source desktop apps for parallel coding agents, compared on licence, telemetry, planning and checks, with sources.
summary: Keyboard-first, AGPL, free, strong on Windows, WSL and remote control.
answer: Pane and Ninebrains are both free, open-source desktop apps that run coding agents in parallel, one git worktree each. Choose Pane for a keyboard-first terminal workflow, WSL support, remote and phone control, and scheduled Loops. Choose Ninebrains for a dependency-aware job graph, checks that block completion until they pass, an Apache-2.0 licence and no telemetry.

what.text: A terminal-first, open-source agent manager for running any CLI agent in parallel.

price.text: Free. No paid plan, seat fee or usage fee.

agents.text: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent, Aider, Goose, or any CLI tool.

isolation.text: One pane per feature, one git worktree each.

planning.text: Pane Chat, a global orchestrator terminal that coordinates agents across panes and worktrees. A task dependency graph is not described.

verification.text: A built-in diff viewer, approvals, and bundled reviewer and verify helper agents. An enforced gate before done is not described.

telemetry.text: Product analytics are on by default, through PostHog, and can be tied to your GitHub username or git email. You can turn them off in Settings.

chooseThem.text: You work keyboard-first in terminals, or on Windows through WSL.
You want to drive agents on a remote machine from the desktop, a browser or your phone.
You want agents on a schedule: Loops run an agent on a cron schedule in a fresh worktree.

chooseUs: You want a plan with dependencies, dispatched to idle lanes, rather than coordinating agents by chat.
You want completion blocked until configured checks pass, with three attempts before a job blocks.
You want Apache-2.0 rather than AGPL-3.0, or no product analytics at all.
